title: Swiss Steak
subtitle: Braised beef in a thick tomato and vegetable sauce
excerpt: Tenderised braising steak slow-cooked in a rich tomato sauce with onions and peppers. Swiss steak has nothing to do with Switzerland; the name comes from the swissing technique of pounding and rolling the meat.
sourceNotes: American comfort food classic. The term 'swissing' refers to a textile process of passing fabric through rollers; applied here to tenderising beef by pounding.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions with plenty of sauce. Thaw overnight and reheat covered in a low oven or on the hob.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well in a larger pot. Leftovers improve in flavour overnight.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make entirely a day ahead. Reheat covered at 160C for 30 minutes.

content.text: Swiss steak is braised beef cooked in tomato sauce until it collapses into tenderness. Pound the meat first so it absorbs the sauce as it cooks. It needs a long, slow time in the oven; rushing it will leave the beef tough.
Heat the oven to 160C. Use a meat mallet to pound each steak piece to about 1.5cm thick. This breaks the fibres and helps the sauce penetrate.
Coat the steaks in the seasoned flour, pressing it in on both sides. Shake off any excess.
Heat the oil in the dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown the steaks for 3 minutes per side until deep golden. Remove and set aside.
Reduce the heat. Add the onion, pepper, and celery. Cook for 8 minutes until softened, scraping up any browned bits.
Add the garlic and paprika. Stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the tomatoes, stock, and Worcestershire sauce. Add the bay leaves. Bring to a simmer and nestle the steaks back in.
Cover with a lid and transfer to the oven. Cook for 2 hours until the beef is tender enough to cut with a spoon. Remove the bay leaves and serve.

items.symptom: The beef is still tough after 2 hours.
items.cause: The oven was too hot or the cut was very thick.
items.fix: Return to the oven for another 30 minutes at 150C. Braising steak needs time; more heat will not help.

items.cause: The lid trapped too much steam.
items.fix: Remove the lid for the last 20 minutes to let the sauce reduce. Or uncover and simmer on the hob briefly.

items.cause: This is normal. The flour thickens the sauce as it braises.
items.fix: Nothing to fix. If the sauce is still thin, remove the meat and reduce the sauce on the hob for a few minutes.
